Shares of Monde Nissin [MONDE 9.81 11.3%] [link] were briefly halted on Friday after MONDE disclosed that its board had voted to restructure its equity. The board approved a measure that would eliminate a P7.2 billion deficit in stockholder’s equity using, in MONDE’s words, “paid-in capital in excess of par value”. The deficit was created by the massive P20.5 billion negative revaluation of MONDE’s alternative meat business. MONDE said that this equity restructuring is meant to “zero out the Deficit as of December 31, 2022”. Ok, but what’s a deficit? This one is weird if you aren’t familiar with financial statements. When a company makes a profit, whatever is not distributed to shareholders is registered on the balance sheet as “Retained Earnings” in the Shareholder’s Equity section. When a company loses enough money to push this account into the negative, as MONDE did, then the account is shown as a “Deficit” in place of the Retained Earnings account. This is the number that MONDE is hoping to “zero”. But where does the money come from? The account that the “money” is being taken from is the Additional Paid-In Capital account, which is the money that investors paid for MONDE stock that is in excess of the stock’s par value. This account is also in the Stockholder’s Equity section of the Balance sheet. MONDE’s shares have a par value of P0.50/share, it sold 3.6 billion shares for P13.50/share during its IPO, so this account has nearly P47 billion in it. So what happened? Since both accounts are in the Stockholders Equity section of the balance sheet, MONDE is just doing a paper accounting move to get rid of that negative retained earnings balance. Instead of having P46,515,846,865 in Additional Paid-In Capital and a Deficit of P7,153,900,753, they’ll have an Additional Paid-In Capital of P39,361,946,112 and a Deficit of P0.00, which I guess they’d now call a Retaine
